speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the consultation. I understand you are experiencing psychiatric symptoms alongside a new movement disorder; to help me understand your condition, how would you describe the specific movements you are seeing, such as tremors, rigidity, or involuntary jerking?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful; since the movement disorder began two months after starting risperidone, it is likely an extrapyramidal side effect. To distinguish between acute dystonia and akathisia, can you describe if the movements are painful muscle spasms or an intense inner urge to keep moving?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms of an intense inner urge to move, fidgeting, and an inability to sit still are classic signs of akathisia. Did you notice if this restlessness started shortly after beginning your risperidone two months ago?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Recently diagnosed with schizophrenia. No other significant past medical history. Social history: College student, lives with parents. Denies tobacco, alcohol, or drug use.
